title: Food Safety Basics
summary: Safe minimum internal temperatures from USDA, plus clean, separate, cook and chill: the habits the recipes here rely on.

p: Color is not a reliable sign of doneness. Use a food thermometer in the thickest part of the food, away from bone, fat and gristle.

rows: Beef, pork, veal and lamb steaks, chops and roasts
140°F if packaged in a USDA-inspected plant; 165°F for all others
All poultry (breasts, whole birds, legs, thighs, wings, ground poultry, giblets, stuffing)

list: **Clean**: wash your hands with plain soap and water for at least 20 seconds, including the backs, between the fingers and under the nails. Wash utensils and counters often.
**Separate**: use one cutting board for produce and foods eaten raw, and another for raw meat, poultry and seafood. Do not rinse raw meat, poultry, eggs or seafood; it spreads germs.
**Cook**: use a food thermometer and the temperatures above.
**Chill**: refrigerate perishable food within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F). Fridge 40°F or below, freezer 0°F or below. Thaw in the fridge, not on the counter.
Cool big batches quickly: divide soups, rice and casseroles into shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours.
Most cooked leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Plan to eat or freeze prep-day food within that window.
Pack cold lunches with an ice pack in an insulated bag. For hot lunches, fill an insulated food jar with boiling water for a few minutes, empty it, then add food heated to 165°F.
